assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy moved from basic gut-hormone biology to transformative treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefit now documented in large outcome trials. The originality, clarity and breadth of impact on human disease are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Four credited people; a prize allows at most three. Drucker (GLP-1 biology, GLP-2) and Holst (physiology of GLP-1 and incretin effect) are central; Knudsen represents the translation to long-acting analogues. Mojsov's contribution to GLP-1 sequence/activity and its credit are contested as far as I recall; I cannot verify this independently.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple drug classes, years of real-world use and outcome trials; recognition is timely and arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should reward basic physiology only or include industrial drug development.
Disputed credit for Mojsov versus Habener and others; the Habener group is not in the credited list.
Long-term safety of broad obesity use is still accruing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a dominant driver in rheumatoid arthritis and that its blockade produces clinical remission established the cytokine-targeted paradigm for chronic inflammatory disease and changed outcomes for millions of patients. From a clinical autoimmunity viewpoint the impact is large and durable.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly led the conceptual and clinical translation (mechanistic studies, anti-TNF trials in RA) and form a clean pair. Others (e.g. antibody developers, Vilcek, Cerami, Kollias) have claims that the supplied credit does not include.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: more than two decades of use, multiple agents and biosimilars, extensive independent confirmation across indications.
uncertainties: Competing claims for credit on TNF biology and antibody engineering beyond the credited pair.
Possible overlap with later cytokine-pathway recognition (IL-6) in how the committee frames the field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells that durably eradicate refractory B-cell malignancies opened a new therapeutic modality (living drugs) with approved products and extension to other tumors and autoimmune disease.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (CAR design, costimulation) and June (clinical translation and CD19 CAR-T in leukemia) are decisive; Rosenberg's adoptive-cell-therapy and early CAR trials are important but arguably adjacent. Others such as Eshhar are not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature given approvals and a decade of clinical follow-up, though durability data and the solid-tumor frontier are still developing.
uncertainties: Allocation among June, Sadelain, Rosenberg and uncredited pioneers such as Eshhar.
Toxicity, cost and limited efficacy in solid tumors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defined how cytosolic DNA is sensed and linked to type I interferon and inflammation, explaining mechanisms in infection, cancer immunity, and interferonopathies and autoimmune disease such as lupus. It is a conceptually clear innate-immunity discovery with broad relevance.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP as the second messenger, a decisive contribution; Barber discovered STING. Other credited names (Sun, Wu, Ishikawa) were part of these discoveries, with Ishikawa also linked to STING; I judge Chen and Barber the cleanest pair.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is widely confirmed; therapeutic translation (STING agonists/antagonists) has not yet delivered approved drugs, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Credit between Barber, Ishikawa and Chen's group for STING is not fully settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cloning and characterization of IL-6 and the successful therapeutic blockade of its receptor (tocilizumab) established a second major cytokine-targeted route in rheumatoid arthritis, giant cell arteritis, cytokine release syndrome and more.
assessment.attribution: Kishimoto and Hirano are the recognized discoverers of IL-6 (B-cell stimulatory factor 2) and the receptor biology; Kishimoto led the therapeutic antibody effort. The pair is coherent.
assessment.maturity: Mature: approved drug in use for years with independent trials, including use in COVID-19 and CAR-T toxicity.
uncertainties: Hirano's relative contribution to the clinical translation.
Whether the committee would pair this with TNF, which would affect timing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of activity with light and changed experimental physiology across fields. The discovery and engineering of channelrhodopsin and its use in neurons is a strong example of a tool that enabled many discoveries.
assessment.attribution: Six credited people. Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterized channelrhodopsin; Deisseroth led neuronal application and tool development. Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck have significant claims, so any three-person split is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a method; clinical use is still emerging (e.g. vision restoration), which matters for a medicine prize.
uncertainties: Whether a research tool without direct clinical consequence fits the Physiology or Medicine criteria as strongly as therapy-defining work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle vaccines against HPV are a rare case of a basic discovery producing demonstrated cancer prevention, with population data showing reduction of high-grade cervical lesions and invasive cancer.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the L1 VLP approach; Frazer made key contributions to VLP vaccine development. Others such as Zhou and Kirnbauer are not in the credited list, so allocation is a concern, and zur Hausen was already recognized for the HPV-cancer link.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: population-level evidence of effectiveness is now strong.
uncertainties: Competing credit among several groups with independent VLP work.
Prior prize for HPV-cervical cancer link could make the committee weigh the vaccine less.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 as an inhibitor of cell death, linked from the t(14;18) translocation to the apoptosis pathway and to venetoclax, is foundational for cancer biology and targeted therapy.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams (BCL-2 family biology, Emu-myc and BCL-2 work) and Vaux (BCL-2 function in cell death) are central; Strasser is a major later contributor but a fourth name. Tsujimoto and Korsmeyer are not credited, and I recall Tsujimoto's cloning of the translocation as relevant, which would complicate allocation.
assessment.maturity: Mature given venetoclax approval and extensive confirmation, and the apoptosis field has been recognized before (Brenner, Horvitz, Sulston), which may reduce the case.
uncertainties: Allocation among four credited names plus uncredited pioneers.
Possible view that apoptosis has already been recognized.
